title: Social clubs he belonged to and which declined
summary: He lists the clubs he belonged to while in the ballroom business, which ones went down, and the Zulus, Bethlehem and Eclipse.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well let me ask you about the societies and clubs that you belong to. How many of you belong to in your life?
Well in my life I belong to, used to belong to Tisha Mingos.

Mmhmm. Eclipse Aiden Pleasure Club. Frogs. I used to be back at the National Park on Willow in Thuid. I belong to the, used to belong to the bulls. I used to belong to the money wasters. The original spokes. Oh I, uh, Zulus. Yeah Tammany. I used to be in all them things when I had some money. And none of them I didn't used to belong to because I was always in the ballroom business and that made you belong to them because they helped you out. But at that time I had money then. I ain't got no money to take care of all of them now.
Well some of them went down huh?
Oh yeah, a whole lot of them went down.
Which ones went down that you remember?

Well uh, the Eclipse they went down, the Frogs they went down, the Bulls went down, and the Money Wasters went down and come back up again. And uh, and Tammany, uh, they didn't ever go out but they was down, I think they're down now altogether. And the Zulus, they went down. See, and they're down now but what I mean, they get the body of people that perform the carnivals. You see, like any club wanna come in, can go in and help them on the carnival but they had not a big outfit like they used to be. See, see what I mean, at one time the Zulus was independent than the other club. But all them members died out from there. And them did die out there. They're just out and don't worry with it.
I think that some Bethlehem Society helps the Zulus.
The Bethlehem, yeah that's uh, Bethlehem, that's the society from downtown. Yeah, Bethlehem. Yeah, they do, on Connerville, they do help them.
And uh, when they have to have them?

Well, originally, they are, uh, any club can go in. Now, they ask for any club to come help. Even to this, over here, if they wanna turn out with them, they can't turn out. See, they don't pick no, no kind of club not to turn out. Cause you, you got a club that can't turn out on Connerville.
I'm not sure about this, but as I remember, I've been to anniversaries and funerals both, with the Zulus, where they have the Bethlehem with them. It seems strange.
Well, the Bethlehem was a, was a little side club they had down there. And, uh, that club started in, uh, what you call, I think it was, they had a place they called a Tin Top on Padilla and Liberty.

Franklin, Franklin. I think they had a place they used to call a Tin Top. I think the Bethlehem started in there. And they had another one down there named Clover. The Clover. Remember the Clover? Eh? Well, the Clover used to have meat up in there. It was just a, ballroom, but, uh, that's where they started from up in there. Bethlehem already did go out with Zulu.
Now, the Eclipse, did that have anything to do with Eclipse Alley?

No. No, that was Eclipse Social Aid and Pleasure Club. That was, that was at, uh, Fultz and Ferret. Uh, Buddy Blissett, he was, he was the president of that at that time. At that time we used horses in carriages when they would parade. See, we didn't have no automobiles, they'd use carriages. So, that was back in, oh, way back in 1950s, 60s.
